evidence: Experiments are performed using C4.5, Ripper and a Naive Bayes classifier.
We experimented on nine different datasets.
%FP and %TP were averaged over 10-fold cross-validation runs for each of the data combinations.
Out of a total of 48 experiments performed, SMOTE-classifier does not perform the best only for 4 experiments.
unresolved: n_seeds is inferred from '10-fold cross-validation' repetition, not a stated seed/trial count; paper never uses the word 'seed'.

n_eval_types (3) groups AUC, ROC-curve/ROC-convex-hull, and Acc+/Acc- as the distinct evaluation metrics reported for SMOTE's own results; precision/recall are discussed only in the related-work IR section, not used to evaluate SMOTE itself, so excluded.

n_baselines (7) counts plain majority under-sampling, Ripper loss-ratio variation, Naive Bayes prior variation, minority over-sampling by replication, C4.5 decision-threshold tuning, one-sided selection, and the SHRINK system; boundary is fuzzy since some (e.g. threshold tuning) are variants of the same base classifier rather than distinct external methods.

control_arm is a poor fit for this paper's design (it is a class-imbalance/resampling paper, not an adversarial/backdoor paper with a clean-vs-poisoned split), so set to 'none' rather than forcing 'clean'.
